 President Trump signed an executive order creating a women's health task force and a division at the National Institutes of Health to advance research, diagnostics, and treatments for women's health issues.
 Updated: 5:36 PM EDT Oct 19, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Rachel Hirschheimer Washington Correspondent WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump signed an executive order Monday aimed at improving women's health outcomes, establishing a women's health division at the National Institutes of Health and a White House women's health task force. 
 "Today's order also establishes the White House women's health task force, which will mobilize the entire federal government to coordinate action focused on improving women's health," Trump said. 
 Advertisement The initiative, led by First Lady Melania Trump, aims to promote new research, advance diagnostic technology, and improve treatments for women's health issues, including cardiovascular disease and maternal health. 
 "Previous generations fought for women's rights. Our generation will fight to discover the cures that will ensure a woman can live her life in health and to the fullest," Melania Trump said. 
 The issue of women's health has recently gained bipartisan support. Last month, the Senate held its first hearing on menopause, addressing gaps in research, training, and care. 
 Dr. Rachel Rubin , a urologist and sexual medicine specialist, highlighted the challenges and opportunities presented by the executive order. 
 "It's going to require heavy funding. It's going to require businesses to be interested and manufacturers to be interested. It's going to require research support, and it's going to require a lot of advocacy, and I think there's bipartisan support for this, and so it's a real opportunity for everybody to lead in this space and really make some big changes," Rubin said. 
 The women's health task force was expected to hold its first meeting today at the White House.
